Children learn everything at school that matters in a job. After school you do not have to go on learning.
Everyone has to stop working earlier because everything is changing.
284.context: Because the skills jobs need change quickly, adults have to go on learning after their training. This is called lebenslanges Lernen, lifelong learning.

285.text: Ms Frost works as a permanent employee in an office. What does she not have to pay out of her salary?
285.context: Value added tax is paid on purchases, not deducted from wages. Income tax and social insurance contributions are.

286.text: Which body in a company helps employees with problems with their employer?
286.context: The works council, the Betriebsrat, represents employees in dealings with the employer and is elected by the workforce.

287.text: You want to end your employment with a company in Germany. What do you have to observe?
287.context: When you resign you have to observe the notice period, the Kündigungsfrist, set out in your contract or by law.

288.text: What is the basis of Germany's special responsibility for Israel?
options: the National Socialist crimes against Jews
the Basic Law of the Federal Republic of Germany
288.context: Germany's special responsibility for Israel arises from the National Socialist crimes against Jews, above all the murder of six million people in the Holocaust.

289.text: A man with dark skin applies for a job as a waiter in a restaurant in Germany. What is an example of discrimination? He does not get the job solely because …
options: his German is not good enough.
his salary expectations are too high.
he has no experience in the job.
289.context: Refusing someone a job solely because of dark skin is racial discrimination and forbidden.

290.text: You have bought a television in Germany. At home you unpack the television, but it does not work. The television is broken. What can you do?
options: make a complaint about the television
290.context: A broken new appliance can be returned as faulty — you make a complaint, a Reklamation, and can ask for repair or replacement.

291.text: Why do you have to state on your tax return in Germany whether you belong to a church or not? Because …
options: there is a church tax that is linked to income tax and wage tax.
this is important for statistics in Germany.
you have to pay more tax if you do not belong to a church.
the church is responsible for the tax return.
291.context: Church tax is collected together with income tax, so the tax return has to record whether you belong to a church that levies it.

292.text: People in Germany live by the principle of religious tolerance. What does that mean?
options: Everyone can believe what they want.
The state decides which god people believe in.
292.context: Religious tolerance means everyone may believe what they wish, or nothing at all. The state does not prescribe a faith.

293.text: What is an Easter custom in Germany?
293.context: Painting eggs, and hiding them for children to find, is the classic German Easter custom.

294.context: Whitsun, Pfingsten, is a Christian holiday celebrated fifty days after Easter. Whit Monday is a public holiday in Germany.

295.text: Which religion has shaped European and German culture?
295.context: Christianity has shaped European and German culture most strongly, visible in holidays, churches, art and music.

296.text: In Germany, the last four weeks before Christmas are called …

296.context: The four weeks before Christmas are Advent. Many families light one candle on an Advent wreath each Sunday.

297.text: Which country have most migrants to Germany come from?

298.text: The migrants living in the GDR came above all from …
298.context: Migrants in the GDR came mainly from other socialist states, above all Vietnam, Poland and Mozambique, usually as contract workers.

299.text: Foreign workers recruited by the Federal Republic of Germany in the 1950s and 1960s were called …
299.context: Workers recruited abroad in the 1950s and 1960s were called Gastarbeiter, guest workers. Many stayed and made Germany their home.

300.text: Which country did the first guest workers in the Federal Republic of Germany come from?
